_comment: Watch pages. One entry renders one page at /videos/<slug>/ whose only subject is one clip, which is what Google asks for before a video is eligible for video results, Video mode and key moments. `key` is the media key in data/media.json, so the clip itself, its poster, its dimensions and its duration are never restated here. Adding an entry is all it takes to give another clip a watch page: build.py picks it up, the VideoObject on every other page that embeds the clip is repointed at it, and the video sitemap entry moves with it. `chapters` are read off the recording frame by frame; do not add one that has not been checked against the footage.

pages.title: A 3D scene graph built live from one RGB camera, ScanNet scene 0000
pages.metaTitle: 3D scene graph from one camera, ScanNet scene 0000
pages.description: M2H-MX predicts depth and semantics from a single RGB stream while Mono-Hydra++ builds a hierarchical 3D scene graph of ScanNet scene 0000 in real time.
pages.standfirst: Ten seconds of screen recording at sixteen times real time. One image stream goes in, and a layered map of a whole apartment comes out, with no depth sensor and no LiDAR anywhere in the loop.

sections.heading: The input is one image stream
sections.text: Three views run down the right of the frame: the raw RGB frame from ScanNet scene 0000, the semantic labels M2H-MX predicts from it, and the depth M2H-MX predicts from the same frame. Those predictions are everything the map is built from. No depth camera and no LiDAR appear anywhere in this recording.

sections.heading: The map is a graph, not a point cloud
sections.text: The structure on the left hangs from a single building node. A room node sits under it, a layer of place nodes under that marking the free space the camera has moved through, and below those the object boxes, labelled bed, cabinet, desk and table, standing on the reconstructed RGB mesh. Every layer is attached to the one above it, so a query can go from a room to the objects inside it without searching the mesh.

sections.heading: It is built while the camera moves
sections.text: Mono-Hydra++ takes the two predictions into its visual-inertial odometry and its mapping backend as they arrive, so the graph in the recording is the state of the map at that instant rather than a reconstruction assembled afterwards. Playback is sixteen times real time.

pages.title: A drone flies one corridor loop and the 3D scene graph builds itself
pages.metaTitle: 3D scene graph over one drone corridor loop, ITC building
pages.description: M2H with Mono-Hydra builds a hierarchical 3D scene graph from one camera and an IMU while a drone flies a loop of the ITC building second floor.
pages.standfirst: Forty-two seconds at ten times real time, from the first frame to loop closure. A camera and an IMU go in; a mesh, objects, places and rooms come out, and the corridor circuit closes on itself.

sections.heading: One loop of a real building
sections.text: The recording follows a drone through a single circuit of the second floor of the ITC building at the University of Twente. The camera stream, the semantic labels M2H predicts from it, and the predicted depth run down the right of the frame throughout, and the map on the left is built from those predictions alone.

sections.heading: Five layers, built together
sections.text: Eight seconds in, the recording labels the layers: the building node at the top, the room nodes under it, a layer of semantic places, the object boxes below those, and the 3D RGB mesh at the bottom. The mesh extends along each corridor as the drone passes down it, and room nodes appear under the building node as the circuit turns.

sections.heading: Loop closure
sections.text: In the last seconds the view turns top down and the circuit meets itself. The two ends of the corridor join, and the graph is corrected into one consistent floor instead of a drifting chain of corridors.
